readings.title: The puddle that drew attention
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: After rain, a large puddle regularly formed outside an adult learning centre. Visitors blamed a blocked drain. Before ordering repairs, the caretaker photographed the area after several storms and marked where water first gathered. He found that a recently raised flower bed directed water away from its former path. The drain itself was clear. A small opening in the bed's border restored the flow and reduced the puddle. Photographs taken before and after the change helped the centre explain the decision to residents. The case showed how repeated observation could prevent an expensive response to the wrong cause.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: Numbers without a comparison
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A neighbourhood group reported that its garden received thirty millimetres of rain in one week. The number attracted attention, but readers asked whether it was unusual. The group had measured only for a month, so it could not answer from its own records. A nearby long-running station provided a useful comparison, although its different location meant the figures were not directly interchangeable. The group published both sets with a short explanation of the difference. Members learned that presenting a number clearly also involves explaining the comparison that gives it meaning and the limits of that comparison.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: A volunteer's empty notebook
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: During a summer monitoring project, Ewan missed three visits to a pond. Embarrassed by the gaps, he considered entering estimates based on neighbouring days. The project leader advised against it. Missing observations, she explained, were different from measurements of zero and different from guesses. Ewan marked the dates as unobserved and briefly recorded why. When researchers later examined the records, they could see exactly where uncertainty remained. The leader also changed the rota so volunteers could request cover in advance. An honest gap was more useful than a complete-looking record whose apparent precision concealed information that had never been collected.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: The stream's two banks
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Two groups sampled a stream on the same afternoon and obtained different results. Instead of arguing about whose figures were correct, they walked through their methods together. One group had taken water from a shallow sunny edge; the other had sampled a deeper shaded point. The project then defined a shared sampling position and asked each team to record time and conditions. Differences did not vanish, but they became easier to interpret. The exercise turned a disagreement into a discussion of method. Comparable observations required more than using instruments with the same brand name.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

translation.stem:
Translate this original passage into Chinese.

Careful observation begins with a question, but it also requires patience with uncertain answers. A surprising measurement should lead us to examine the method as well as the event itself. Recording where, when and how information was collected allows other people to understand its limits. Such detail turns a private impression into evidence that can be discussed.
translation.referenceAnswer: 仔细观察始于一个问题，但也需要耐心面对不确定的答案。一个出人意料的测量结果，应促使我们既检查事件本身，也检查测量方法。记录信息收集的地点、时间和方式，能让他人理解其局限。这些细节使个人印象成为可以讨论的证据。
translation.explanation: 参考译文展示一种可接受的表达；保留原文信息及逻辑、中文通顺的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write about 120 English words for this original simulation task.

Your adult study club plans a month of local weather observations. Write instructions covering a consistent routine, the handling of missed observations and the way results should be presented.
writing.sampleAnswer: Our club will record rainfall at the same place each morning for one month. Everyone should first practise reading and emptying the collector with the coordinator. Please note the date, time and any unusual conditions before sharing the reading. If you cannot attend, ask the group for cover in advance. When nobody makes an observation, mark the date as missing rather than entering a guess or a zero. At the end of the month, we can prepare a graph with clear units and visible gaps. The accompanying note should explain our method and the short period covered. We may describe what we observed, but should avoid claiming that one month's figures establish a long-term trend.
writing.explanation: 范文用于作答后参考；观点与例子可以不同，但须回应全部要求并表达清楚。
